title: fix(fixtures): a flipped setup's fixtures are judged against the carried stock's shape, not its box
body:
Branched from upstream main.

## What changed

The check for fixtures in a carried setup (`app::fixture_carried`) used to judge each fixture by its world bounding box. A vise's box spans the opening between its jaws. A soft-jaw nest pocket sits inside the jaws' box. So a part clamped between the jaws, or seated in the nest, was reported as "standing inside the stock carried from Setup 1", and the post was refused (#1530: 4.48 mm and 11.43 mm deep).

- **Box first, then mesh.** The box is still the first check. When it flags a fixture, the fixture's closed world mesh is then read column by column against the carried stock. For each column it takes the Z spans the mesh puts on the column's vertical line and compares them with the column's material.
  - The line reading is the new `FixtureMesh::steel_on_line` in `crates/sim/src/fixture_mesh/column.rs`.
  - It uses signed crossings with the same nonzero/odd-parity rule as the existing point-in-solid test.
  - Touching or overlapping shells merge into one span.
  - An ambiguous line (one through a facet edge, or one lying in a wall face) is nudged by one millionth of the mesh's scale, capped at 0.1 micron a step, and read again.
  - A line whose winding goes negative or does not close at zero (an inside-out shell over another) is not read: the box stands.
- **Between the columns, read whole (review rework).** Every rectangle spanned by four neighbouring material columns, trimmed by the contact tolerance, is judged against the material the four share by the new `FixtureMesh::steel_in_prism` (`crates/sim/src/fixture_mesh/prism.rs`). Facets clipped to the rectangle that reach into the material slab convict. With no facet over the rectangle, there is no steel there. Otherwise the slab holds no surface, and one line decides whether it is all steel or all air. Nothing inside the material is sampled, so a post or a lip narrower than the pitch is refused. Where the four columns disagree (a side face or a step runs through), only what they share is judged: a boundary is known to one pitch, as with the box law.
- **Contact tolerance.** A column is refused only when the overlap is more than `CARRIED_CONTACT_TOL` (0.01 mm). That must hold on the centre line and on four lines 0.01 mm beside it, so a face that lies exactly on a column centre counts as contact.
- **The mesh can only clear a fixture, never add a hit.** In these cases the box depth stands, as before:
  - an open or refused mesh;
  - a coarse-fidelity fixture (#864);
  - a line that no nudge can read, or that winds inconsistently;
  - a rectangle between the columns that cannot be read;
  - a spent facet-visit budget (`MESH_VISIT_BUDGET`, 50 M visits per fixture, logged when it runs out);
  - a footprint narrower than one grid cell.
- **Bounded time.** A column or rectangle whose box depth cannot exceed the worst depth already found is skipped. A fixture that really penetrates therefore stops after its first refused column.
- **Refusal text.** A fixture that really enters the carried material is still refused by name with its depth, in the same message as before.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1530-carried-fixture-shape.md`.

## How tested

New `crates/app/tests/carried_fixture_shape.rs`:
- **Setup.** A 50 x 50 x 10 part in 56 x 56 stock. Setup 1 contours its sides down to Z 4, leaving a 3 mm brim (the hat). Setup 2 flips it over X (AlignPartToSetup FlipX) and faces the brim side. In Setup 2 the section stands at Z 0..6 and the brim at Z 6..10.
- **Pins.** Each also checks that the post gate reports the same lines:
  - `the_flipped_hat_enters_setup2_section_down_brim_up`: the fixture geometry is real, and the grid pitch is under 0.5 mm.
  - `a_builtin_vise_gripping_the_flipped_parts_sides_is_held`: built-in 5 in vise, jaws 5 mm high, faces at Y ±25, floor at Z 0. Accepted.
  - `a_vise_jaw_moved_into_the_part_is_refused_by_name_with_its_depth`: opening 48. Refused, `5.00 mm deep`.
  - `soft_jaws_whose_nest_clears_the_part_are_held`: one-piece soft jaws (5 shells) whose pocket clears the part by 0.05 mm. Accepted.
  - `soft_jaws_with_a_nest_too_small_are_refused_by_name_with_the_depth`: pocket 0.5 mm too small on each side. Refused, `fixture 'Soft jaws' ... setup 'Setup1' ... 5.00 mm deep`.
  - `a_nest_floor_a_hair_past_the_contact_tolerance_is_refused`: nest floor 0.03 mm into the part, 0.02 mm past the tolerance. Refused, `0.03 mm deep`.
  - `a_nest_floor_touching_within_the_contact_tolerance_is_held`: floor 0.005 mm into the part. Accepted.
  - `a_post_narrower_than_the_pitch_between_the_columns_is_refused`: the review's 0.19 x 0.19 post, 3 mm in, on no column line. Refused, `3.00 mm deep`.
  - `a_lip_narrower_than_the_pitch_between_the_columns_is_refused`: the review's 0.19 x 48 lip, 4 mm in. Refused, `4.00 mm deep`.
  - `an_open_mesh_keeps_the_box_verdict`: the clear nest with one facet removed. Refused, `5.00 mm deep` (box).
  - `a_coarse_fidelity_fixture_keeps_the_box_verdict`: the clear nest flagged coarse (#864). Refused, `5.00 mm deep` (box).

New `crates/app/tests/carried_fixture_guards.rs` calls `mesh_penetration` on hand-built carried bodies, so each guard is reached on its own:
- `an_unread_column_line_keeps_the_box_depth` (budget 0 gives the box depth)
- `an_inside_out_shell_between_the_columns_keeps_the_box_depth`
- `a_post_between_the_column_lines_is_steel`
- `a_fixture_narrower_than_a_cell_off_the_lines_keeps_the_box_depth`
- `a_face_on_a_column_centre_where_the_material_ends_is_contact`
- `a_rectangle_reads_its_contact_band_at_the_tolerance` (second review): a block mid-cell, 0.03 mm into the material, refused `Some(0.03)`; 0.005 mm, `None`.
- `a_rectangle_is_trimmed_by_the_tolerance_only` (second review): a 0.015 mm post at x 1.512..1.527 (past the line at 1.51), refused `Some(3.0)`.
- `a_pitch_too_fine_to_trim_keeps_the_box_between_the_columns` (second review): at a 0.015 mm pitch, a 0.003 mm post 3 mm in mid-cell is refused at 3.0, as the box refuses it.

Second review, also in `carried_fixture_shape.rs`: `a_turned_setup_judges_its_fixture_in_the_turned_frame`, a 60 x 30 bar with Setup2 turned 90 degrees about Z (not flipped). A pocket fitting the turned brim is held; 1 mm short it is refused `4.00 mm deep`; the same pocket read in the unturned frame would be refused 10 mm deep (checked by hand).

**Slim rectangles (second review).** Below a 0.02 mm pitch the rectangle trimmed by the tolerance inverts. It is now tested as slim before the off-footprint `continue` (which an inverted rectangle always took, clearing it), so it is unread and keeps the box depth. The line and prism readings' other early-outs were re-read: a facet index the mesh does not hold now reads unread (both), and a non-finite clip reads as steel over the slab, so neither can clear.

New `crates/sim/tests/fixture_mesh_column.rs` tests `steel_on_line` directly:
- block span / miss
- a line on a facet diagonal is nudged and read
- nest pocket vs wall, with touching shells merged
- a line in a wall face is still read
- a spent budget reads nothing
- non-finite input is not read
- an inside-out shell over another is not read as air (the review's A 0..10 / B 5..15 reversed)
- a 6 micron block at X 5000 is read where it stands (capped nudge)
- a budget cut mid-line never reads part of a line
- `steel_in_prism`: a post no line meets is steel; a box wholly inside steel is steel; contact band; budget, NaN and inverted input are unread

The existing `carried_fixtures_cache.rs` passes unchanged, including the sub-cell dowel-pin pin.

### Mutation checks
The full table (the review's M1-M10 plus the rework's guards) is in the PR comment for head 87f657fa; the second review's P2b, P2c and P5 are now red (PR comment for head a4befa9b). Every guard is red under its mutation except two: M5 (centre line only) is stricter, not looser, and G2 (the winding must close at zero) is a defensive guard that only a partial reading reaches, and the budget guard pinned by M4 already catches that.

### Performance (release, M-series Mac, re-measured after the second review)
- Pins: `carried_fixture_shape` 0.59 s debug for all 12. `carried_fixture_guards` under 0.01 s.
- 400 k-facet fixtures: a 100 k-segment cylinder whose cap fans every line and rectangle near the centre meets, plus a tall block so the box flags every column (radius 3-9.5 mm, pitch 0.2-1.0 mm).
  - With no limit: up to 13.8 s (449 M visits).
  - With the 50 M-visit budget the time is the budget times the cost of a visit: 0.33 s when the visits are line reads, 1.6-2.2 s when they are rectangle clips (the worst seen). M3 measured 0.74-0.80 s on its construction. A spent budget keeps the box verdict, logged.

## Gates
On head a4befa9b (merges cleanly with upstream main):
- App, all green: lib 194; carried_fixture_shape 12; carried_fixture_guards 8; carried_fixtures_cache 7; accessory_collisions 2; builtin_vise 9; fixture_* (keys_lenient, law_gaps, library, locate, locate_stock, mesh, mesh_posed, plate, plate_detect, plate_followups, plate_riders, route, ux); fixtures 14; posting 17; setup_carry 9; verify 21; verify_arc_reading 7.
- Sim, all green: lib 146; fixture_mesh_column 12; fixture_mesh_convict 5; fixture_mesh_posed 9 (1 ignored); posed_band_cylinder 3.
- Sim also: fixture_mesh 9 (1 ignored), fixture_arc_sagitta 10, fixture_stack_span 8, posed_fixture 7, posed_fixture_midpose 3, c_axis_fixture 8.
- Clippy `-D warnings`: `-p camcraft-app --all-targets` clean. `-p camcraft-sim` lib and fixture_mesh_column clean. The sim `--all-targets` run stops on a lint already on main in `fixture_mesh_convict.rs`, a file this PR does not touch.

## Not exercised
- The MCP `add_builtin_vise` replay of the user's h5 project; the pins rebuild the same geometry headlessly.
- A real STEP soft-jaw import.
- Inside the material nothing is sampled. At a side face or a step, contact is resolved to the carried grid's pitch, as with the box law: steel at most one pitch into the material at the face, short of the next column centre, can pass. The M3 review found the side verdicts equal to main's at every phase and ruled it non-blocking; it is stated in the decision record and filed as #1580 (P7).
- A strip 0.02 mm wide (2 x the contact tolerance) along each column line is read only by the five lines: a wall thinner than that lying on a line passes. This is the contact tolerance by design and is stated in the decision record.
- Seen while building the pins and not followed up: in 60 x 60 stock, a 15.24 mm contour around a 50 x 50 part left the stock's outer corners (about 1.5 mm triangles) at full height in the carried body. The pins use 56 x 56 stock. This may need its own issue.

Changelog: A flipped (carried) setup's fixtures are judged by their real shape against the stock carried from the earlier setup, so a vise gripping the part's sides or soft jaws with a nest are no longer refused; steel truly inside the carried part is still refused with its depth.

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1530
